title: 2026 edition REPORT
overview: Mobile app trends: 2026 edition A global benchmark of mobile app performance, combining industry context and 2026 marketing themes with performance analyses of gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps. The report uses aggregated, anonymized data from apps tracked by Adjust from January 2024 to January 2026, alongside some third-party industry estimates. A global benchmark of mobile app performance, covering overall industry trends and gaming, e-commerce/shopping, and finance apps, with regional analysis including APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America. Performance trends are reported for January 2024–December 2025, including year-over-year comparisons for 2024 and 2025.
methods: Uses Adjust data to report app installs and sessions globally, with monthly trends from January 2024 to December 2025 and year-over-year comparisons for 2024–2025. The excerpts do not specify the app sample frame or a validation method.
key_findings: There were more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025.
Global consumer spending on apps rose to $167 billion in 2025.
Mobile technologies and services are projected to generate 8.4% of global GDP by 2030.
Eight of the top 10 mobile games in 2025 each generated more than $1 billion in player spending.
The global mobile-gamer population reached nearly 3 billion in 2025, representing more than 80% of the global gaming population.
Gaming app installs in MENA grew 2% year over year in 2025.
limitations: The report says GenAI maturity varies: most organizations report low or moderate maturity, while efficiency gains over 20% are reported only for a small group with advanced deployment.
The report describes finance apps’ shift toward paid acquisition as likely linked to falling costs, rather than establishing the cause.
For some gaming categories, sessions fell despite install growth; the report says churn may need to be addressed.

sections.section_label: Introduction: Evolution and opportunity in the mobile app industry
sections.summary: Introduces the growth outlook for mobile apps and the measurement and marketing challenges created by fragmented channels, evolving user behavior, and AI. It frames the report as a benchmark for gaming, e-commerce, and finance.
key_points: The report cites more than 112.1 billion app downloads in 2025, an estimated 5.8 billion unique smartphone users, and consumer spending of $167 billion, up 10.6% year over year.
It describes experimentation with AI, automation, and channel diversification as key features of 2025, while emphasizing the need for actionable data and cross-channel attribution.

sections.section_label: AI transforms from strategic tool to core infrastructure in 2026
sections.summary: Describes AI being integrated into marketing and measurement workflows through data-analysis assistants, predictive audience segmentation, and practical generative-AI use. It notes that organizational maturity remains uneven.
key_points: AI assistants can query multi-channel data in natural language and surface analysis, reports, and visualizations in real time.
Audience segments are shifting from manually maintained static lists to dynamic groups based on behavior, intent, and likelihood to convert.

sections.section_label: Mobile-first approach evolves into multi-platform strategy
sections.summary: Argues that customer journeys now move across mobile web, desktop, apps, and other channels, making cross-platform measurement and deep linking important for attribution and conversion.
key_points: Only around 31% of marketers report complete satisfaction with their ability to unify and read data across platforms.
Cross-platform measurement connects activity such as a mobile-web session to an in-app conversion, revealing channel contributions beyond last-click credit.
The report recommends integrated measurement, high-quality deep linking, user segmentation, retargeting, and web-to-app solutions to reduce journey barriers.

sections.summary: Summarizes selected year-over-year findings across the three app verticals and explains the report’s dataset, coverage, regions, and date range.
key_points: The takeaways report global e-commerce app sessions increased 5%; LATAM finance installs and sessions rose 76% and 57%; and gaming retention remained flat, with day 1 at 27% and day 30 at 5%.
The methodology covers e-commerce/shopping, finance/fintech, and gaming across global, APAC, Europe, LATAM, MENA, and North America.
The dataset combines Adjust’s top 5,000 apps with the total set of apps tracked by Adjust, with data sources covering 45 countries and approximately 250 countries under the ISO 3166-1 standard.
